arxiv-2004-09508.title: Adversarial Distortion for Learned Video Compression
arxiv-2004-09508.creator: Vijay Veerabadran, Reza Pourreza, Amirhossein Habibian, Taco Cohen
arxiv-2004-09508.description: Abstract In this paper, we present a novel adversarial lossy video compression model. At extremely low bit-rates, standard video coding schemes suffer from unpleasant reconstruction artifacts such as blocking, ringing etc. Existing learned neural approaches to video compression have achieved reasonable success on reducing the bit-rate for efficient transmission and reduce the impact of artifacts to an extent.

arxiv-2104-10446.title: Lacon-, Shrub- and Parity-Decompositions: Characterizing Transductions of Bounded Expansion Classes
arxiv-2104-10446.creator: Jan Dreier ORCID:https://orcid.org/0000-0002-2662-5303
arxiv-2104-10446.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jan Dreier ORCID:https://orcid.org/0000-0002-2662-5303. The concept of bounded expansion provides a robust way to capture sparse graph classes with interesting algorithmic properties. Most notably, every problem definable in first-order logic can be solved in linear time on bounded expansion graph classes. First-order interpretations and transductions of sparse graph classes lead to more general, dense graph classes that seem to inherit many of the nice algorithmic properties of their sparse counterparts.

arxiv-2105-07339.title: The role of non-axisymmetry of magnetic flux rope in constraining solar eruptions
arxiv-2105-07339.creator: Ze Zhong, Yang Guo 🖂, M. D. Ding 🖂
arxiv-2105-07339.description:
A 2021 arXiv research paper by Ze Zhong, Yang Guo 🖂, M. D. Ding 🖂. Abstract

Whether a solar eruption is successful or failed depends on the competition between different components of the Lorentz force exerting on the flux rope that drives the eruption. The present models only consider the strapping force generated by the background magnetic field perpendicular to the flux rope and the tension force generated by the field along the flux rope.

arxiv-2202-01834.title: The exact solution of the Axial Next - Nearest - Neighbor Ising model on width 2 spin chains
arxiv-2202-01834.creator: Pavel Khrapov, Anastasia Loginova
arxiv-2202-01834.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Pavel Khrapov, Anastasia Loginova. Using the transfer matrix method for Axial Next-Nearest Neighbor Ising model without an external field on a closed chain of spins of width 2 in the direction of interaction of only nearest neighbors and length L L in the direction of interaction of nearest neighbors and next nearest neighbors, we found exact values of the partition function in a finite strip of length L L , free energy, internal energy per node, heat capacity in a finite strip of length

arxiv-2206-01513.title: Electron Mass Singularities in Semileptonic Kaon Decays
arxiv-2206-01513.creator: Chien-Yeah Seng 1, William J. Marciano 2, Ulf-G. Meißner 1,3,4
arxiv-2206-01513.description: Abstract We show that recent improvements in the O ⁡ ( α ) O(\alpha) long-distance quantum electrodynamics (QED) corrections to the radiative inclusive K e ​ 3 K_{e3} decay rate using the Sirlin representation are free from infrared divergences and collinear electron mass singularities in the limit m e → 0 m_{e}\rightarrow 0 , as predicted by the Kinoshita-Lee-Nauenberg theorem.

arxiv-2206-06479.title: Robust Distillation for Worst-class Performance
arxiv-2206-06479.creator: Serena Wang, Harikrishna Narasimhan, Yichen Zhou, Sara Hooker, Michal Lukasik, Aditya Krishna Menon
arxiv-2206-06479.description: Abstract Knowledge distillation has proven to be an effective technique in improving the performance a student model using predictions from a teacher model. However, recent work has shown that gains in average efficiency are not uniform across subgroups in the data, and in particular can often come at the cost of accuracy on rare subgroups and classes.

arxiv-2212-14567.title: Topical Hidden Genome: Discovering Latent Cancer Mutational Topics using a Bayesian Multilevel Context-learning Approach
arxiv-2212-14567.creator: Saptarshi Chakraborty, Zoe Guan, Colin B. Begg, Ronglai Shen
arxiv-2212-14567.description: Abstract Statistical inference on the cancer-site specificities of collective ultra-rare whole genome somatic mutations is an open problem. Traditional statistical methods cannot handle whole-genome mutation data due to their ultra-high-dimensionality and extreme data sparsity – e.g., >30 million unique variants are observed in the ~1700 whole-genome tumor dataset considered herein, of which >99% variants are encountered only once.

arxiv-2310-03638.title: Huge Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions in Pt/Co/Re thin films
arxiv-2310-03638.creator: Amar Fakhredine ID, Andrzej Wawro, Carmine Autieri ID
arxiv-2310-03638.description: Abstract We investigate the magnetization and the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions (DMI) in Pt/Co/Re thin films in the case of perfect interfaces and upon the introduction of intermixing on both Co interfaces. Calculations were implemented on a series of systems with a varied number of cobalt atomic layers (ALs).

arxiv-2310-19743.title: Tell Me What Is Good About This Property: Leveraging Reviews For Segment-Personalized Image Collection Summarization
arxiv-2310-19743.creator: Monika Wysoczanska, Moran Beladev, Karen Lastmann Assaraf, Fengjun Wang, Ofri Kleinfeld, Gil Amsalem, Hadas Harush Boker
arxiv-2310-19743.description: Abstract Image collection summarization techniques aim to present a compact representation of an image gallery through a carefully selected subset of images that captures its semantic content. When it comes to web content, however, the ideal selection can vary based on the user’s specific intentions and preferences. This is particularly relevant at Booking.

arxiv-2404-12706.title: On balanced homodyne measurement – simple proof of wave function collapse
arxiv-2404-12706.creator: E. Brüning a and S. Nagamachi b b The University of Tokushima, Tokushima 770-8506, Japan
arxiv-2404-12706.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by E. Brüning a and S. Nagamachi b b The University of Tokushima, Tokushima 770-8506, Japan. Using only elementary calculus we prove that the balanced homodyne detector measures the quadrature phase amplitude of a signal. More precisely, after the measurement of photon numbers l l , the collapse of the composite state of a strong laser beam and a signal approximates the collapse of the signal to the eigen-state of quadrature phase amplitude with eigen-value r r .

arxiv-2409-18451.title: Concave tents: a new tool for constructing concave reformulations of a large class of nonconvex optimization problems
arxiv-2409-18451.creator: Markus Gabl
arxiv-2409-18451.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Markus Gabl. Optimizing a nonlinear function over nonconvex sets is challenging since solving convex relaxations may lead to substantial relaxation gaps and infeasible solutions that must be "rounded" to feasible ones, often with uncontrollable losses in objective function performance. For this reason, these convex hulls are especially useful if the objective function is linear or even concave, since concave optimization is invariant to taking the convex hull of the feasible set.

arxiv-2412-02593.title: Generalized Yamabe Flows
arxiv-2412-02593.creator: Jørgen Olsen Lye, Boris Vertman, Mannaim Gennaro Vitti
arxiv-2412-02593.description: Abstract . In this work we introduce a family of conformal flows generalizing the classical Yamabe flow. We prove that for a large class of such flows long-time existence holds, and the arguments are in fact simpler than in the classical case.

arxiv-2504-01835.title: Autonomous optical navigation for DESTINY + \text{DESTINY}^{\text{+}} : Enhancing misalignment robustness in flyby observations with a rotating telescope
arxiv-2504-01835.creator: Takayuki Hosonuma, Takeshi Miyabara, Naoya Ozaki, Ko Ishibashi, Yuta Suzaki, Peng Hong, Masayuki Ohta, Takeshi Takashima
arxiv-2504-01835.description: Abstract DESTINY + \text{DESTINY}^{\text{+}} is an upcoming JAXA Epsilon medium-class mission to flyby multiple asteroids including Phaethon. As an asteroid flyby observation instrument, a telescope mechanically capable of single-axis rotation, named TCAP, is mounted on the spacecraft to track and observe the target asteroids during flyby.

arxiv-2504-20636.title: Quasiperiodic Slow-Propagating EUV “Wave” Trains After the Filament Eruption
arxiv-2504-20636.creator: Yining Zhang, Ting Li, Weilin Teng, Xinping Zhou, Yijun Hou, Zheng Sun, Xuchun Duan, Yilin Guo, Guiping Zhou
arxiv-2504-20636.description: Abstract The eruption of the filament/flux rope generates the coronal perturbations, which further form EUV waves. There are two types of EUV waves, including fast-mode magnetosonic waves and slow waves. In this paper, we first report an event showing the Quasiperiodic Slow-Propagating (QSP) EUV “wave” trains during an M6.

arxiv-2505-16849.title: Walk&Retrieve: Simple Yet Effective Zero-shot Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Knowledge Graph Walks DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: Information Retrieval’s Role in RAG Systems; July 17, 2025; Padua, Italy CCS: Information systems Information retrieval CCS: Information systems Language models CCS
arxiv-2505-16849.creator: Martin Böckling, Heiko Paulheim, Andreea Iana
arxiv-2505-16849.description: Abstract . Large Language Models (LLMs) have showcased impressive reasoning abilities, but often suffer from hallucinations or outdated knowledge. Knowledge Graph (KG)-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) remedies these shortcomings by grounding LLM responses in structured external information from a knowledge base.

arxiv-2507-23003.title: Characterization of spurious-electron signals in the double-phase argon TPC of the DarkSide-50 experiment Journal: Eur. Phys. J. C
arxiv-2507-23003.creator: The DarkSide-50 Collaboration a,1 {}^{\text{a,1}}
arxiv-2507-23003.description: Abstract Spurious-electron signals in dual-phase noble-liquid time projection chambers have been observed in both xenon and argon Time Projection Chambers (TPCs). This paper presents the first comprehensive study of spurious electrons in argon, using data collected by the DarkSide-50 experiment at the INFN Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso (LNGS).

arxiv-2510-13523.title: Weak unipotence and Langlands duality
arxiv-2510-13523.creator: Jia-jun Ma, Shilin Yu
arxiv-2510-13523.description: Abstract . Weak unipotence of primitive ideals is a crucial property in the study of unitary representations of reductive groups. We establish a sufficient condition, referred to as mild unipotence , which guarantees weak unipotence and is more accessible in practice.

arxiv-2511-06748.title: Image Restoration via Primal Dual Hybrid Gradient and Flow Generative Model Thanks: Corresponding author.
arxiv-2511-06748.description: Abstract Regularized optimization has been a classical approach to solving imaging inverse problems, where the regularization term enforces desirable properties of the unknown image. Recently, the integration of flow matching generative models into image restoration has garnered significant attention, owing to their powerful prior modeling capabilities.

arxiv-2511-21376.title: Informed Burn-In Decisions in RAR: Harmonizing Adaptivity and Inferential Precision Based on Study Setting
arxiv-2511-21376.creator: Lukas Pin *, Stef Baas, Gianmarco Caruso, David S. Robertson, Sofía S. Villar
arxiv-2511-21376.description: Abstract Response-Adaptive Randomization (RAR) is recognized for its potential to deliver improvements in patient benefit. However, the utility of RAR is contingent on regularization methods to mitigate early instability and preserve statistical integrity. A standard regularization approach is the “burn-in” period, an initial phase of equal randomization before treatment allocation adapts based on accrued data.

arxiv-2512-07780.title: The heartbeat of stellar halos: Insights from the stellar halo mass-metallicity relation
arxiv-2512-07780.creator: Jenny Gonzalez-Jara ,, Patricia B. Tissera, Antonela Monachesi, Brian Tapia-Contreras, Susana Pedrosa, Rosa Domínguez-Tenreiro, Lucas Bignone
arxiv-2512-07780.description: Abstract Context. The stellar halo mass–metallicity relation (MZhR) has been observed in nearby Milky Way–mass galaxies and explored in numerical simulations. Recent advances in understanding stellar halo assembly, both observationally and theoretically, motivate the investigation of whether the MZhR is already in place at high redshift. Aims.

arxiv-2601-17636.title: HealDA: Highlighting the importance of initial errors in end-to-end AI weather forecasts
arxiv-2601-17636.creator: Aayush Gupta, Akshay Subramaniam, Michael S. Pritchard, Karthik Kashinath, Sergey Frolov, Kelsey Lieberman, Christopher Miller, Nicholas Silverman, Noah D. Brenowitz
arxiv-2601-17636.description: Abstract Machine-learning (ML) weather models now rival leading numerical weather prediction (NWP) systems in medium-range skill. However, almost all still rely on NWP data assimilation (DA) to provide initial conditions, tying them to expensive infrastructure and limiting the practical speed and accuracy gains of ML.

europmc-pmc5509825.description: Camouflaging of autistic characteristics in social situations is hypothesised as a common social coping strategy for adults with autism spectrum conditions (ASC). pmc-10622493.title: Multifractal analysis of cellular ATR-FTIR spectrum as a method for identifying and quantifying cancer cell metastatic levels
pmc-10622493.creator: Ayan Barbora, Sirish Karri, Michael A. Firer, Refael Minnes
pmc-10622493.description: Cancer is a leading cause of mortality today. Sooner a cancer is detected, the more effective is the treatment. Histopathological diagnosis continues to be the gold standard worldwide for cancer diagnosis, but the methods used are invasive, time-consuming, insensitive, and still rely to some degree on the subjective judgment of pathologists.

pmc-10683584.title: Identification and diagnostic potential of serum microRNAs as biomarkers for early detection of Alzheimer’s disease
pmc-10683584.creator: Ying-Hao Han, Hong-Yi Xiang, Dong Hun Lee, Lin Feng, Hu-Nan Sun, Mei-Hua Jin, Taeho Kwon
pmc-10683584.description: This study aimed to investigate the differential expression of serum microRNAs in cognitive normal subjects (NC), patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and patients with Alzheimer’s disease (AD), with the objective of identifying potential diagnostic biomarkers. A total of 320 clinical samples, including 32 MCI patients, 288 AD patients, and 288 healthy controls, were collected following international standards.

pmc-11414983.title: The risk of dyslipidemia on PLHIV associated with different antiretroviral regimens in Huzhou
pmc-11414983.creator: Yanan Wang, Zhongrong Yang, Jing Li, Zhenqian Wu, Xiaoqi Liu, Hui Wang, Yuxin Chen, Ziyi Wang, Zhaowei Tong, Xiaofeng Li, Feilin Ren, Meihua Jin, Guangyun Mao, Manuela Ceccarelli, Cavin Epie Bekolo, Cavin Epie Bekolo, Cavin Epie Bekolo
pmc-11414983.description: BackgroundDyslipidemia is increasingly common in people living with HIV (PLHIV), thereby increasing the risk of cardiovascular events and diminishing the quality of life for these individuals. The study of blood lipid metabolism of PLHIV has great clinical significance in predicting the risk of cardiovascular disease.

pmc-11716751.title: Development of NULISA™ CNS Disease Panel 120 for comprehensive proteomic profiling of neurodegenerative diseases
pmc-11716751.creator: Xiao‐Jun Ma, Shweta Iyengar, Shalaka Deshmukh, Roopa Comandor, Sean Kim, Xiaomei Xu, Xioalei Qiu, Bingqing Zhang, Yuling Luo
pmc-11716751.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe development of reliable blood biomarkers for neurodegenerative diseases (NDDs) has been hindered by the lack of tools with sufficient sensitivity to detect low concentrations of brain‐derived proteins in plasma or serum in a highly multiplexed manner. NULISA™ (NUcleic acid‐Linked Immuno‐Sandwich Assay) has emerged as a promising solution, with attomolar sensitivity and capable of high multiplexing in a fully automated system.

pmc-12490221.title: Dynamic multi-omics profiling of islet and gut hormonal secretion and peripheral crosstalk in response to various nutrient loads
pmc-12490221.creator: Jiachen Wang, Ling Liu, Hechun Liu, Yu Qian, Sijie Zhang, Shuai Zheng, Hemin Jiang, Yue Zhou, Xiaoliang Cheng, Qi Fu, Hao Dai, Tao Yang
pmc-12490221.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). SummaryPostprandial metabolism is a complex and dynamic process involving diverse biomolecules, with islet and gut hormones playing crucial roles. However, how these hormones interact with biomolecules after nutrient intake and coordinate with peripheral insulin resistance (IR) remains elusive. This study characterizes postprandial multi-omics dynamics under mixed meals and four distinct macronutrient loads, investigating hormone secretion patterns, associated responsive molecules, and their relationships with IR.
